---
title: "Community Water Fluoridation and Adult Tooth Loss"
author: "Michael Warnick"
date: "2026-11-17"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Background
Community water fluoridation means adding a small amount of fluoride to
public drinking water to help prevent tooth decay.

In 2025, Utah became the first state to ban fluoride in public drinking water, and Florida followed soon after.

**Question:** Do states where more people drink fluoridated water have lower rates of tooth loss in adults?

## The Data

*This is simulated (fake) data for practice.*

```{r data}
fluoride = tibble(
  state           = c("Utah", "Idaho", "Colorado", "Arizona", "California", "Oregon",
                      "Texas", "Florida", "Georgia", "Ohio", "Illinois", "Minnesota",
                      "New York", "Maine", "New Jersey"),
  region          = c("West", "West", "West", "West", "West", "West",
                      "South", "South", "South", "Midwest", "Midwest", "Midwest",
                      "Northeast", "Northeast", "Northeast"),
  pct_fluoridated = c(55, 35, 70, 55, 60, 25, 75, 75, 95, 90, 98, 98, 70, 80, 15),
  pct_teeth_lost  = c(38, 43, 34, 39, 37, 44, 40, 41, 35, 33, 32, 30, 36, 35, 45)
)

knitr::kable(fluoride)
```
## Summary by Region

```{r region-summary}
region_avg = fluoride %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(avg_fluoridated = mean(pct_fluoridated),
            avg_teeth_lost  = mean(pct_teeth_lost))

knitr::kable(region_avg, digits = 1)
```

The Midwest has the most fluoridation and the least tooth loss.
## Fluoridation vs. Tooth Loss

```{r scatter}
fluoride %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pct_fluoridated,
             y = pct_teeth_lost)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = region), size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "More Fluoridation, Less Tooth Loss",
       x = "Population on fluoridated water (%)",
       y = "Adults 65+ who lost 6+ teeth (%)",
       color = "Region") +
  theme_minimal()
```
As fluoridation goes up, tooth loss goes down.

## Statistical Analysis

```{r model}
mod1 = glm(pct_teeth_lost ~ pct_fluoridated, data = fluoride)
summary(mod1)
```

The p-value for `pct_fluoridated` is below 0.05, so fluoridation is
significantly related to tooth loss.

## Conclusions

- States with more fluoridation have lower adult tooth loss in this data.
- This uses fake data; the final project will use real CDC data.
- Next step: add a U.S. map of fluoridation by state.
